'''Derrick Dewayne Zimmerman''' (born December 2, 1981) is an American  [[basketball]] coach and former player. He is currently the associate head coach at the [[Louisiana-Monroe Warhawks men's basketball|University of Louisiana-Monroe]]. Zimmarman played [[college basketball]] at [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State University]].

==College career==
For the Mississippi State Bulldogs, he averaged 8.9 points, 5.5 assists, 4.2 rebounds, 1.9 steals and 0.8 blocks. He shot 15 of 52 three-pointers as a senior and 64.9% on free throws.

==Professional career==
He was selected 40th overall in the [[2003 NBA draft]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]], and played two games with the [[NBA]]'s [[New Jersey Nets]] during the [[2005-06 NBA season|2005–06 season]].<ref>[http://www.basketballreference.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=ZIMMEDE01 NBA stats at Basketballreference.com] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060629105343/http://basketballreference.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=ZIMMEDE01 |date=June 29, 2006 }}.</ref>

Those two games ended up being Zimmerman's only playing time in the NBA. His 2nd game ever (also his final NBA game ever) was played on April 19, 2006, in a 83–90 loss to the [[New York Knicks]] where he recorded 4 points, 5 assists and 1 rebound.

He played in the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]] for the [[Columbus Riverdragons]] (2004–05) and [[Austin Toros]] (2005–06). Derrick was named the NBDL's Defensive Player of the Year for two consecutive seasons (Austin 2005–06, Columbus 2004–05).<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/215546/Derrick-Zimmerman-Signs-With-BC-Kyiv Derrick Zimmerman Signs With BC Kyiv].</ref> In December 2006, he signed a one-month contract with [[Brose Baskets]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]].<ref>[http://admin.euroleague.net/eurocup/news/i/3187/brose-baskets-signs-zimmerman-at-point Brose Baskets signs Zimmerman at point].</ref> After his contract expired, he signed with Italian team [[Air Avellino]] until the end of the season.

In the summer of 2008, he signed with the Ukrainian club [[BC Budivelnyk|Budivelnyk Kyiv]]. He stayed in Ukraine till 2013, and later played with [[BC Hoverla|Hoverla Ivano-Frankivsk]], [[BC Kyiv|Kyiv]] and [[BC Dnipro-Azot Dniprodzerzhynsk|Dnipro-Azot]].

In February 2013, Zimmerman moved to Germany and signed with [[Neckar Riesen Ludwigsburg]] for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/99589/neckar-riesen-ludwigsburg-announced-derrick-zimmerman.html Neckar Riesen Ludwigsburg announced Derrick Zimmerman].</ref> In January 2014, after a couple months without a club, he signed with [[Energa Czarni Słupsk]] of Poland for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/cat/nba/110883/energa-czarni-sign-derrick-zimmerman.html Energa Czarni sign Derrick Zimmerman].</ref>

==Coaching==
===Mississippi State (2018-2020)===
After his playing career, Zimmerman returned to his alma mater, Mississippi State, in 2018, serving two seasons as a graduate assistant and one as director of scouting and analytics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Derrick Zimmerman - Men's Basketball Coach |url=https://hailstate.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/derrick-zimmerman/2431 |website=Mississippi State |access-date=19 December 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

===Louisiana (2021-2025)===
In 2021, Louisiana head coach [[Bob Marlin]] hired Zimmerman as an assistant coach.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ragin' Cajuns men's basketball adds Derrick Zimmerman as an assistant coach |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/acadiana/sports/ul_lafayette/ragin-cajuns-mens-basketball-adds-derrick-zimmerman-as-an-assistant-coach/article_df84cc76-ce10-11eb-bbbb-639ee01ffded.html |access-date=19 December 2024 |work=The Advocate |date=15 June 2021 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Derrick Zimmerman - Men's Basketball Coach |url=https://ragincajuns.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/derrick-zimmerman/1703 |website=Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns |access-date=19 December 2024 |language=en}}</ref> On December 19, 2024, amid a 3–9 start to the season, Louisiana fired Marlin and named Zimmerman the interim head coach for the remainder of the 2024-25 season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Foote |first1=Kevin |title=Bob Marlin fired in 15th season as UL men's basketball coach a day after winning a game |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/acadiana/sports/ul_lafayette/bob-marlin-fired-in-15th-season-as-ul-mens-basketball-coach-a-day-after-winning/article_641393a0-be54-11ef-8cdb-c7ffbdb53e3b.html |access-date=19 December 2024 |work=The Advocate |date=19 December 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

===Louisiana-Monroe (2025-present)===
In April 2025, Zimmerman was hired as the associate head coach for the [[Louisiana-Monroe Warhawks men's basketball|University of Louisiana-Monroe]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://ulmwarhawks.com/news/2025/4/14/mens-basketball-cunningham-announces-coaching-staff-additions.aspx| title=Cunningham Announces Coaching Staff Additions| website=ulmwarhawks.com| date=April 14, 2025| access-date=October 26, 2025}}</ref>
